other_failure_modes.name: Ordinal encoding for MLP without embeddings
other_failure_modes.description: Categorical variables are encoded using OrdinalEncoder and fed directly into a linear layer (MLP) as continuous float values. This incorrectly imposes an arbitrary ordinal relationship on categorical data; one-hot encoding or entity embeddings should be used for neural networks.

other_failure_modes.name: DataLoader multiprocessing without __main__ guard
other_failure_modes.description: Using PyTorch DataLoader with num_workers > 0 in a script that executes training at the top level (without an if __name__ == '__main__': block) can cause the script to hang indefinitely or crash on systems using 'spawn' for multiprocessing (like macOS and Windows).

summary: The agent provides a structurally sound PyTorch MLP solution with correct data splitting and leakage-safe preprocessing. However, it critically fails by feeding ordinally encoded categorical variables directly into the MLP as continuous values, introducing spurious ordinal relationships. Additionally, it lacks feature engineering, evaluates the stochastic model only once, relies solely on accuracy as a metric, and risks execution hangs due to PyTorch multiprocessing without a main guard.
